{{short description|Italian mathematical statistician}}
'''Sonia Petrone''' is an Italian mathematical statistician, known for her work in Bayesian statistics, including use of [[Bernstein polynomial]]s for [[nonparametric statistics|nonparametric methods]] in [[Bayesian statistics]].{{ran|RBP}}{{ran|BDE}}{{ran|CPP}} With Patrizia Campagnoli and Giovanni Petris she is the author of the book ''Dynamic Linear Models with R'' (Springer, 2009).{{ran|DLM}}

==Education and career==
Petrone earned a [[laurea]] in [[economic]] and [[social sciences]] from [[Bocconi University]]. She completed her Ph.D. in 1989 at the [[University of Trento]]. After working at the [[University of Pavia]] from 1991 to 1998, and at the [[University of Insubria]] from 1998 to 2001, she became a full professor of statistics at Bocconi University.{{r|bocconi}}

Petrone was the president of the [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]] for the 2014 term.{{r|past}} She was a co-editor of the journal Bayesian Analysis (2010–2014) and the editor of the journal ''[[Statistical Science]]'' for 2020–2022.{{r|statsci}}

==Recognition==
With Sara Wade and Silvia Mongelluzzo, Petrone won the Lindley Prize of the [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]] in 2010.{{r|lindley}} She was a Medallion Lecturer of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] for 2018.{{r|medallion}} She is also a Fellow of the [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]],{{r|fisba}} and an Elected Member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].{{r|isi}} She was named to the 2022 class of Fellows of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], for "significant and impacting contributions to the foundations of Bayesian statistics and Bayesian nonparametric inference and prediction, as well as long-standing professional service and dedicated mentoring throughout her career".{{r|fims}}
